pairs.answer: A fuel-fed fire produces thick black smoke, while an oil-fed fire produces bright orange flames

pairs.question: How can a pilot distinguish an oil-fed engine compartment fire from a fuel-fed engine compartment fire, and what action addresses an oil-fed fire?
pairs.answer: Increasing airspeed is the recommended method to stop an oil-fed fire

pairs.question: How can a pilot distinguish an oil-fed engine compartment fire from a fuel-fed engine compartment fire, and what action addresses an oil-fed fire?
pairs.answer: Shutting off the electrical master switch is the primary action for an oil-fed fire

pairs.question: How can a pilot distinguish an oil-fed engine compartment fire from a fuel-fed engine compartment fire, and what action addresses an oil-fed fire?
pairs.answer: An oil-fed fire is identified by white smoke and requires immediate engine restart
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.15 – Engine Fire

pairs.question: How can a pilot distinguish an oil-fed engine compartment fire from a fuel-fed engine compartment fire, and what action addresses an oil-fed fire?
pairs.answer: Feathering is never an acceptable method to stop propeller rotation during an oil-fed fire
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.15 – Engine Fire

pairs.question: How can a pilot distinguish an oil-fed engine compartment fire from a fuel-fed engine compartment fire, and what action addresses an oil-fed fire?
pairs.answer: Placing the mixture to full rich is the correct response to an oil-fed engine fire
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.15 – Engine Fire

pairs.question: How can a pilot distinguish an oil-fed engine compartment fire from a fuel-fed engine compartment fire, and what action addresses an oil-fed fire?

pairs.source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.15 – Engine Fire

pairs.question: How can a pilot distinguish an oil-fed engine compartment fire from a fuel-fed engine compartment fire, and what action addresses an oil-fed fire?
pairs.answer: Both oil-fed and fuel-fed fires are identified solely by the color of the engine cowling discoloration
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.15 – Engine Fire

pairs.question: What are important considerations regarding the electrical master switch and structural integrity during an in-flight engine compartment fire?
pairs.answer: Shutting off the electrical master switch prevents use of panel radios for transmitting distress messages
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.15 – Engine Fire

pairs.question: What are important considerations regarding the electrical master switch and structural integrity during an in-flight engine compartment fire?
pairs.answer: Deactivating the electrical system causes ATC to lose transponder returns

pairs.question: What are important considerations regarding the electrical master switch and structural integrity during an in-flight engine compartment fire?
pairs.answer: Even a brief but intense engine fire could cause dangerous structural damage to the wing

pairs.question: What are important considerations regarding the electrical master switch and structural integrity during an in-flight engine compartment fire?
pairs.answer: The electrical master switch should always be the first item shut off during any engine fire
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.15 – Engine Fire

pairs.question: What are important considerations regarding the electrical master switch and structural integrity during an in-flight engine compartment fire?
pairs.answer: Transponder returns are unaffected when the electrical master switch is turned off
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.15 – Engine Fire

pairs.question: What are important considerations regarding the electrical master switch and structural integrity during an in-flight engine compartment fire?
pairs.answer: Structural damage from an engine fire is only a concern for twin-engine airplanes

pairs.question: What are important considerations regarding the electrical master switch and structural integrity during an in-flight engine compartment fire?
pairs.answer: An engine fire that appears extinguished will not rekindle once airspeed is stabilized

pairs.question: What are important considerations regarding the electrical master switch and structural integrity during an in-flight engine compartment fire?
pairs.answer: Pilots of twin-engine airplanes must always divert immediately regardless of fire status
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.15 – Engine Fire

pairs.question: What are important considerations regarding the electrical master switch and structural integrity during an in-flight engine compartment fire?
pairs.answer: Panel radios operate independently of the electrical master switch during emergencies
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.15 – Engine Fire

pairs.question: What are important considerations regarding the electrical master switch and structural integrity during an in-flight engine compartment fire?
pairs.answer: Wing structural failure from fire is only possible if flames are visible to the pilot
pairs.source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.15 – Engine Fire

pairs.question: What are important considerations regarding the electrical master switch and structural integrity during an in-flight engine compartment fire?
pairs.answer: The electrical master switch should be shut off only if the airplane is equipped with a fire suppression system
